findings.title: Prevent late private responses from undoing account restore
findings.suggested_fix: Stop renewing credentials on arbitrary private/status responses. Serialize renewal and identity-changing requests across tabs through response consumption. Preserve unrelated guest A. Regress delayed A responses after B restore and assert both cookies remain B's.
findings.why_it_matters: A delayed guest-A response can overwrite restored account-B cookies because A remains valid. Client epoch checks run after the browser applies Set-Cookie and cannot prevent the reversal.

findings.title: Include the auth overlay in scheduled retention jobs
findings.suggested_fix: Share approved auth/erasure overlay selection with run-retention-job.sh, including credentials needed for linked-account retries when login is off. Reinstall the timer executable and test both cleanup modules with synthetic secrets. Keep credentials API/cleanup-only.
findings.why_it_matters: With login enabled, installed retention timers use base Compose without the admin-key overlay. Settings fails before history cleanup or pending linked-account erasure retries run.

findings.title: Declare account problem responses in the generated contract
findings.suggested_fix: Declare ProblemResponse and application/problem+json for account errors, replacing the generated 422 declaration. Document applicable domain-error statuses, regenerate contracts and compare runtime bodies/media types with OpenAPI.
findings.why_it_matters: Invalid login input returns 422 application/problem+json with ACCOUNT_INPUT_INVALID, while OpenAPI advertises application/json HTTPValidationError. Typed clients also lack declared authentication, challenge and availability errors.

findings.title: Stopped workers leave expired leases blocking history erasure
findings.suggested_fix: Determine rewrite busy state from unexpired durable send fences under the owner lock. Preserve the complete provider-window allowance. Test worker crash and flags-off cleanup resuming after fence expiry without restarting the worker.
findings.why_it_matters: A crashed worker's leased send-marked job blocks history erasure after its disclosure fence expires. With worker polling stopped, manual clearing and scheduled retention depend on separate recovery that can take 24 hours.

findings.title: Scope Tarot deletion drains to the deleted reading
findings.suggested_fix: Capture only fences for the target tarot_session_id and owner before deletion, preserving the owner lock and post-commit drain. Keep subject-wide capture for profile erasure. Test unrelated sends do not delay reading deletion while its own admitted sends still drain.
findings.why_it_matters: Deleting one Tarot reading drains every rewrite for its owner, including unrelated work. The reading is already deleted when an unrelated provider call can exceed the browser's 15-second timeout; retry then returns not found. Live duration incidence was not measured.
findings.validation_reason: When an unrelated admitted rewrite belongs to the same owner, the new tarot/service.py:262 subject-wide capture and :271 drain delay acknowledgement after the selected reading is deleted, reproduced in memory with an unrelated active fence keeping deletion pending until released, and the permitted 20-60-second provider window exceeds client.ts:403's 15-second DELETE timeout without an override at :658-662, although live duration incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Synchronize erasure proof on committed revocation
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sleep with a bounded wait until find_by_token_hash returns None while provider release stays unset. Then assert erasure remains pending and retain completion, no-resend and spend assertions.
findings.why_it_matters: The erasure test sleeps 100 ms without observing committed revocation. A slow run can leave credentials active while the pending-task assertion passes merely because erasure has not started. PostgreSQL slow-run incidence was not measured.
findings.validation_reason: If erasure has not acquired the owner lock within 100 ms, the newly added test_postgres_concurrency.py:148-160 can pass its pending-task assertion yet read an active credential because guest/postgres.py:118-125 and accounts/postgres.py:60-76 synchronize only after competing operations reach the owner lock, so the fixed sleep does not establish committed revocation and slower-run incidence was not measured on PostgreSQL.

findings.suggested_fix: Test background hiding and persisted pageshow/BFCache revalidation. Keep content hidden until the same owner is verified; changed owners must clear queries and redirect. Verify unmount prevents late rendering/navigation.

triage_groups.title: Auth activation without widening secret access
triage_groups.context: The worker and scheduled cleanup inherit the API's auth flags but need different secret access.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Apply-queue: correct worker IAM overrides (#1), then mirror approved app overlays in the installed retention runner (#5); verify both against the shared production configuration.
triage_groups.why: One role-aware configuration review covers both failures, but each needs a distinct fix.

triage_groups.title: Session transitions and departing screens
triage_groups.context: Cookie renewal ordering and uncancelled guest adoption can undermine deliberate identity changes; boundary lifecycle tests leave returning-page paths uncovered.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Apply-queue: settle cookie/transition serialization (#4), thread cancellation through guest creation and adoption (#12), then cover page visibility/BFCache ownership rechecks (#11).
triage_groups.why: Response ordering is not solved by an epoch check after Set-Cookie; lifecycle tests should exercise the final transition contract.

triage_groups.title: Bounded erasure and evidence of its completion
triage_groups.context: History busy checks, Tarot drain scope, privacy disclosures and a release-test synchronization seam all concern erasure acknowledgement.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Apply-queue: align history busy state with live durable fences (#7), limit reading deletion to its own sends (#9), observe committed revocation in the release test (#10), and align privacy wording with actual linked-identity erasure (#8).
triage_groups.why: Preserve live disclosure barriers and nonrefundable debit history while removing stale or unrelated waits; no item authorizes premature erasure.

If erasure has not acquired the owner lock within 100 ms, the newly added test_postgres_concurrency.py:148-160 can pass its pending-task assertion yet read an active credential because guest/postgres.py:118-125 and accounts/postgres.py:60-76 synchronize only after competing operations reach the owner lock, so the fixed sleep does not establish committed revocation and slower-run incidence was not measured on PostgreSQL.

verdict_reason: Three confirmed P1 defects remain, including an account-restore cookie reversal that violates the project security gate. Required release and activation evidence is incomplete. Fix the actionable queue and verify it before release; keep auth/generation off until separate real-provider and production gates pass.
